\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دقت} (diqqat)}{دقت (diqqat)}]{\ur{دقت} (diqqat) — a difficulty; a hassle}

\label{lesson:UR-C368-diqqat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a clause, then the Urdu for to come into force.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دقت}}
\textbf{\ur{دقت}} — \emph{diqqat} — \textquotedblleft{}a difficulty; a hassle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{کوئی} \ur{دقت} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{مجھے} \ur{بتائیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar koī diqqat hai to mujhe batāiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there is any difficulty, tell me.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دقت}} (\emph{diqqat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{diqqa}, \textquotedblleft{}fineness, exactness\textquotedblright{}; Urdu uses it for a difficulty or a hassle, a sense our sources do not trace.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{diqqat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{diqqat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar koī diqqat hai to mujhe batāiye.} — If there is any difficulty, tell me.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a clause, then the Urdu for to come into force, then say \emph{diqqat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{دقت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A difficulty; a hassle\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رکاوٹ} (rukāvaṭ)}{رکاوٹ (rukāvaṭ)}]{\ur{رکاوٹ} (rukāvaṭ) — an obstacle}

\label{lesson:UR-C368-rukavat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to come into force, then the Urdu for a hassle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رکاوٹ}}
\textbf{\ur{رکاوٹ}} — \emph{rukāvaṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}an obstacle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{رکاوٹ} \ur{آئی} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{دوسرا} \ur{راستہ} \ur{لیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar rukāvaṭ āī to ham dūsrā rāstā leṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If something blocks us, we will take another route.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رکاوٹ}} (\emph{rukāvaṭ}) is built on \textbf{\ur{رکنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to stop\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists beside \emph{roknā} under \emph{*rokk}, \textquotedblleft{}stop\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 10827); \emph{-āvaṭ} makes the noun: what stops you.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حل} (hal)}{حل (hal)}]{\ur{حل} (hal) — a solution}

\label{lesson:UR-C368-hal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a hassle, then the Urdu for an obstacle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حل}}
\textbf{\ur{حل}} — \emph{hal} — \textquotedblleft{}a solution\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{حل} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ملا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{ماہر} \ur{سے} \ur{پوچھیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar hal nahīṅ milā to ham māhir se pūchheṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we find no solution, we will ask an expert.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حل}} (\emph{hal}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥall}, \textquotedblleft{}loosening, solving\textquotedblright{}: untying a knot.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اٹکنا} (aṭaknā)}{اٹکنا (aṭaknā)}]{\ur{اٹکنا} (aṭaknā) — to get stuck; to be held up}

\label{lesson:UR-C368-atakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an obstacle, then the Urdu for a solution.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اٹکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اٹکنا}} — \emph{aṭaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to get stuck; to be held up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{میں} \ur{راستے} \ur{میں} \ur{اٹک} \ur{گیا} \ur{تو} \ur{فون} \ur{کروں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar maiṅ rāste meṅ aṭak gayā to fon karūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If I get stuck on the way, I will phone.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{ٹرک} \ur{پل} \ur{پر} \ur{اٹک} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh ṭrak pul par aṭak gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اٹکنا}} (\emph{aṭaknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{aṭaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to stick\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*aṭṭakk}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 182).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نبٹانا} (nibṭānā)}{نبٹانا (nibṭānā)}]{\ur{نبٹانا} (nibṭānā) — to deal with; to settle (a matter)}

\label{lesson:UR-C368-nibtana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a solution, then the Urdu for to get stuck.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نبٹانا}}
\textbf{\ur{نبٹانا}} — \emph{nibṭānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to deal with; to settle (a matter)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{معاملہ} \ur{نبٹائیں} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{سب} \ur{خوش} \ur{ہوں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp muāmalā nibṭāeṅ ge to sab khush hoṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you deal with the matter, everyone will be happy.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کام} \ur{نبٹایا}, \emph{us ne kām nibṭāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نبٹانا}} (\emph{nibṭānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{nibṭānā}, \textquotedblleft{}finishes\textquotedblright{}, beside \emph{nibaṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be settled\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{nírvartate} (CDIAL 7395). To bring a matter to its end; Urdu also says \emph{nimṭānā}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a solution, then the Urdu for to get stuck, then say \emph{nibṭānā} again
\end{itemize}
